First, I'll parse the SVG path data to identify the vertices and connect them in order.

The path commands:
- M 68.30,63.99 (move to starting point)
- L 51.75,56.30 (line to)
- L 54.65,45.37 (line to)
- L 44.78,49.20 (line to)
- M 44.78,49.20 (move to same point — this creates a discontinuity)
- L 53.45,29.00 (line to)
- L 58.01,38.91 (line to)
- L 72.03,39.79 (line to)
- L 68.30,63.99 (line to — closing back to start)

The "M" command in the middle breaks the path into two separate segments.

Segment 1: 68.30,63.99 → 51.75,56.30 → 54.65,45.37 → 44.78,49.20 (4 points, but last point is repeated due to M)
Segment 2: 44.78,49.20 → 53.45,29.00 → 58.01,38.91 → 72.03,39.79 → 68.30,63.99 (5 points)

Counting unique vertices in order of drawing:
1. (68.30,63.99)
2. (51.75,56.30)
3. (54.65,45.37)
4. (44.78,49.20)
5. (53.45,29.00)
6. (58.01,38.91)
7. (72.03,39.79)
Then back to (68.30,63.99)

That's 7 distinct vertices connected in sequence: 1→2→3→4→5→6→7→1.

A polygon with 7 vertices is a heptagon.

Final answer: (B)
